extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readership interested in international/postwar affairs (policymakers, informed public)
extracted.subtask_description: News reporting on the Allied Foreign Ministers' Conference (Paris) including a proposed draft treaty on the disarmament and demilitarization of Germany, related colonial/trusteeship proposals, and procedural/inspection arrangements. Targets readers of postwar diplomatic/policy developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total disarmament and demobilization of Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: All German forces, including land, air, and naval forces, all para-military forces such as S.S., S.A. and Gestapo, and all organizations auxiliary to the foregoing shall be and shall remain completely disarmed, demobilized and disbanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble and Article I frame this as an essential condition to termination of Allied occupation and as necessary to permit a return to peaceful democratic life; enforcement to continue 'as long as the peace and security of the world require.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on manufacture, production, and importation of military equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: The high contracting parties shall prevent the manufacture, production, or importation of military equipment and devices for military purposes (examples in text include aircraft of all kinds and equipment for anti-aircraft defense).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition is 'subject to the following exceptions and to no others' — the treaty text then lists limited exceptions (e.g., minimal civil police arms). The prohibition extends to facilities, plants and the means to produce such equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and exceptions for German civil police
rubrics_metrics.description: Formation and employment of German civil police and their equipment with such types and quantities of imported small arms as may be essential to the maintenance of public security are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit narrow exception to the general ban on arms; the allowance is limited to minimum quantities/types necessary for public order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive list of military structures and materiel to be abolished or controlled
rubrics_metrics.description: All military structures, all aircraft of all kinds, equipment for anti-aircraft defense, para-military organizations and their staffs, factories, plants, shops and other facilities related to production of war materials are to be disbanded, prevented or controlled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text enumerates categories to be demobilized/disbanded and facilities to be prevented from producing military materiel; the list is intended to be exhaustive except for the stated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention/control of military-related research, technical data and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions, laboratories, testing stations, technical data, patents, plans and drawings related to military production or devices shall be subject to the treaty's control and prevented from being used for military purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The treaty ties control of physical materiel to control of intellectual/technical resources to block rearmament; these elements fall under the inspection and enforcement regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadripartite commission of control (inspection system)
rubrics_metrics.description: To implement disarmament and demilitarization, the high contracting parties agree to provide for a system of quadripartite control: a commission of control which, through its officers and agents, shall conduct, in any and all parts of German territory, such inspections, inquiries and investigations as it may deem necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commission of control has broad authority to inspect anywhere in Germany, determine compliance, and submit reports and recommendations to the high contracting parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, recommendation and enforcement procedures for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the commission has reason to believe a violation has occurred or is about to occur it shall report to the contracting parties and submit recommendations; upon receipt the high contracting parties will, by agreement, take prompt action—including action by air, sea or land forces—to assure immediate cessation or prevention of the violation and shall report to the United Nations Security Council the action taken or to be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mechanism binds the major powers to collective, enforceable responses to violations and requires notification to the UN Security Council; the commission's recommendation drives action taken by unanimous/majority agreement of the high contracting parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Allied Control Council and zonal enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Allied Control Council and the authorities in their respective zones shall enforce strictly the disarmament and demilitarization provisions set forth in Article I; acceptance by Germany of Articles I and II is an essential condition to termination of occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement is both centralized (high contracting parties/commission) and zonal (Allied Control Council in occupation zones), tying political conditions for ending occupation to compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiation of special quadripartite agreements within six months
rubrics_metrics.description: Within six months of the effective date the high contracting parties will consult for the purpose of negotiating special quadripartite agreements which shall provide in greatest practical detail for inspection, inquiry and investigation by the commission of control, for numbers and types of forces which each party shall make available for the purpose, degree of readiness and general location, and for the nature of facilities and assistance which each shall provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These detailed implementation arrangements are to be negotiated quickly and will be subject to ratification by the contracting parties; they operationalize the treaty's inspection and enforcement regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification, deposit, term and renewal of the treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: The treaty shall be ratified by the high contracting parties in accordance with their respective constitutional processes; ratifications shall be deposited and the treaty shall come into force upon deposit by each party. The treaty shall remain in force for a period of twenty-five years and may be renewed, with or without modification, if the interests of international peace and security require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirements for entry into force and an explicit 25-year term (with possible renewal) set the legal/political timeframe for the disarmament regime.
